conversation.message: Less evidence means fewer historical documents or comparative language data points, making it harder to definitively link modern languages to ancient forms without making assumptions. This scarcity of data increases the reliance on educated guesses rather than concrete proof.

conversation.message: For example, reconstructing Proto-Indo-European involves a lot of comparative work across many languages, but the exact sounds and grammar remain partly theoretical.
